(Old Model) Toshiba Canvio 500 GB USB 3.0 Basics Portable Hard Drive (HDTB205XK3AA),Black Okay like so many others reviewing this product, I had a MAJOR problem with it. The drive worked once, then never again. The next times I tried to connect the drive to ANY computer it did not work AND it heated up near the control unit, and led burned out. Thanks to other reviewers, I took their advice and purchased a new drive enclosure, which came with a new cord, leatherette case, and new control unit. Gutted the old Toshiba enclosure, got the drive out and installed it in the new enclosure. 5 Minutes later I was in business. Drive now works on all of my computers.

Toshiba has a real problem here. My theory is they bought a crap load of nbad control units on the cheap, and installed them with their relatively good 1TB drives. Did they recall the drive: NO. Is there any mention of this issue on their site: NO. Any solutions offered by Toshiba: NO, other than return the drive to them ON YOUR $$$! for a "warranty" replacement.

Like so many other tech hardware providers, they hope that attrition will rule the day, and people are too lazy to return things on warranty. In this case your best and fastest solution is to replace the case and forget dealing with Toshiba. Then, NEVER BUY TOSHIBA AGAIN.
text_fidelity_b: (Old Model) Toshiba Canvio 500 GB USB 3.0 Basics Portable Hard Drive (HDTB205XK3AA),Black

text_fidelity_a:
MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black) PROS: Awesome as advertised! Specs and possibly even the parts blow away most high(er)-end laptops in its class...can't beat it for the price. Was debating this over the Samsung Series 7 Gamer with similar specs and both had similar reviews but MSI performed where it counted the most. Better battery, better cooling, mostly better benchmark tests. A big deciding factor for me was that the older MSI GT70 with GTX660/670 still outperformed and outfeatured the Samsung Series 7 Gamer in most of the benchmarking tests...and this next upgrade to MSI GT70 was only $1850 when I bought it...$30 more that the Samsung at the time.

CONS: My only down was with GPU drivers not the actual laptop itself. I think the drivers are so new not even the supposed "BETA" drivers will work with it. It was almost impossible to find the GTX 675m drivers. NVIDIA recommended I get the drivers from the manufacturer's site. And from what I've found there is only one that works and it is on MSI's website. For some reason when I first looked, MSI, didn't have a "notebook" category in their drivers section. It's not even on NVIDIA's site (this had nothing to do with NVIDIA's forums going down, I checked before there forums got hacked).
My reason for purchase.....
First off, I wanted to get this off my chest because I was planning to build a workstation PC (or a powerful PC) but instead switched to getting a laptop. Being that I'm not a laptop fan, I did extensive weeks of research to find the best laptop I could find for my 3d art/animation and gaming needs. Laptop have always been way overpriced and notebook parts can't even touch the PC counterpart; in terms of performance, cooling, etc. Plus, knowing that this an MSI, helped make my decision because they have a good track record of excellent PC parts. I have been building my own desktop PC's for over 10 years and know you get to enjoy the games and 3d applications the way it was meant to be. Also, I'm in the video game development field and needed a second/backup computer/desktop replacement. My current Intel Q9550/Radeon 5700 1GB/ 8GB DDR2 RAM desktop does the JOB but is getting ancient. I was really thinking about getting a workstation or high-end gaming desktop (which would obviously be way cheaper than the most expensive laptop) but after thinking about it, I liked the idea of having the convenience and portability. And, if my desktop goes belly up one day (as it has been acting up) my work flow pipeline won't take a hit. I wont have to deal with the inconvenience of being in a HOT room with 1000W powersupply... even with air conditioning.
text_fidelity_b: MSI G Series GT70 0ND-219US 17.3-Inch Laptop (Black)

text_fidelity_a:
Tram 1185 Amateur Dual-Band Magnet Antenna I bought this Mag-Mount antenna initially for my Boafeng UV-5R+ radio after I bought a SMA-to-SO239/PL259 Connector and I was hitting repeaters over 25 miles away at 5 watts. Later I bought myself a Kenwood TM-281A mobile unit for my car an for the moment it is in use there until I figure out what kind for permanent (drill-in) antenna I want to get for my car. Problem is, this Mag-Mount antenna works so good I am debating on if I really need to get a permanent. Now there are compromises to Mag-Mounts, like cable may not be too long, etc. Eventually I will get a drill-in antenna.

For the TM-281A I have two TX power settings, 65 and 25 watts. This antenna works on both but I couldn't find any documentation on the max power for this antenna so I normally just keep it a 25 watts and it still gets out there just fine.

I would caution to tape around the area where the cable connects to the Mag-Mount to keep moisture out. I haven't have problems yet but I hear that it can be a problem for just about any mag-mounts.

For this price, buy it, test it and if you don't need it, then keep it as a backup.

73'
K9RUM
text_fidelity_b: Tram 1185 Amateur Dual-Band Magnet Antenna

AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices This cord is marketed as a direct replacement to the Garmin power cord. That's why I purchased it. And though it features the compact right angle mini USB plug on one end and provides adequate power to run my 2505LMT, when I plug the cord into the Garmin it immediately reports that the traffic function will not work.

Upon closer examination of the OEM power coed, I observe that it has a blivet on the cord near the 12v plug end that must be the traffic receiver.

This cord has no such receiver and cannot help the 2595LMT receive traffic information.

On the other hand, most of the time traffic information is bogus. And more annoying than useful. The Garmin is constantly binging at me to take an alternate route that never is a better route.

Today I tried following its suggestion to get off the freeway in LA because the Garmin was concerned that the freeway was clogged. It told me to take La Cienega to save 4 minutes. Ha. La Cienega was much, much worse than the freeway and ended up costing me 15 minutes or more. (I think it assumes no one is using surface streets in LA in morning rush hour traffic--a fatal assumption.

Later in the trip it told me the freeway was closed ahead and to take an alternate route. I didn't believe it as I could see with my eyes and the excellent traffic flow in both directions that there was no actual blockage.

So, if you don't mind not having the traffic function, this cord works fine. (And since I don't trust the traffic function, I'll probably turn it off my self -- regardless of cord used.)
text_fidelity_b: AmazonBasics Vehicle Power Cable with Mini-USB Connector for GPS and Other Mini-USB Devices

text_fidelity_a:
Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder This is a good voice recorder. Whether you need it to record your voice memos, lectures, meetings, or discretely record your favorite spy, this will surely be a recorder you'll find many uses for.

It feels very secure in your hand, and has a comfortable feel and weight. It comes with a small pouch, which is nice. The record button is easy to find my sight or feel. The volume and forward/reverse buttons are on an outer button from the record button. Play and stop on the left and index and menu are on the right.

f1 and f2 buttons are primarily used for setting mic sensitivity and voice quality. Under Mic Sensitivity you can choose: Dictate (good for personal memos), Speech recognition (turns on when it hears voice), conversation (good for interviews or conversations, auto zoom (good for large areas where there may be close up voices and far voices), and lecture (good for lectures)

You can choose either low quality at 8kbps in Mp3 format to super high quality 192kbps in mp3. There is also a wave format in 1411 kbps. The higher quality you go impacts total record time. You can add a micro SD card for adding recording time.

There are also 4 index folders labeled A thru D. These are for separating projects. There is also a folder you could place music files if you wanted this to be a mp3 player.

There is also a menu setting where the voice quality and mic sensitivity can be accessed as well as numerous other options such as splitting files, display contrast, and clearvoice (an option that improves the sound quality of the recorded voiec)

The unit comes with rechargable AA batteries that will need to be charged when you first open it. They charge with the included usb to micro USB cord. Any other micro USB cord you own will also work. Once the recorder is connected to your computer through the USB cable you can download and upload voice or mp3 and wave files.

The only thing I wish this had was different settings for each index. For instance I would have liked to set index A for lecture mode at high quality, index B for dictate at a lower quality, etc. Once you set a mic sensitivity and recording quality, they are the same for all index until you change them in settings.

Overall a great quality recorder. Great for meetings, memos, and conversations.
text_fidelity_b: Philips DVT5000/00 4 GB Digital Voice Tracer with 3 Built-in Microphones Voice Recorder

text_fidelity_a:
Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers For years, I used the keyboard kindle after it first came out and loved the "classic" look of the page so much. After replacing it several times due to screen issues, I finally made the switch to the paperwhite with some skepticism, thinking the back-light would make it into yet another screen I look at. I was pleasantly surprised that even the brighter settings still look like a page, and I can turn it all the way down for the same effect as my older model kindle. Plus, I don't need to bother anyone with a light anymore when I read in bed, in the car at night, etc.

Paying a bit extra for no ads was worth it, and I enjoy the drawings that serve as screensavers. The home page is not my favorite - I would prefer to default to my library list instead of wading through recommendations, etc. - but it's not that much of a hassle to tap over to the library screen. When I'm reading a book, it automatically opens to the page I left off on just like my old kindle.

I only vaguely miss having the 3G function my old kindle had because I used to live out in the boonies with limited internet access. However, the WiFi has been generally sufficient and now I just make sure I download a few books before I travel.

Overall, the kindle has definitely revolutionized the way I read since it first came out when I was in high school. I do still keep a lot of hard copies of my favorite series and enjoy reading real books from time to time, but the kindle is SO easy to download anything, anytime you want. Not to mention bringing a whole library with you in one slim package while traveling! I have had this model for a year and a half now, and have no issues or complaints at this time.
text_fidelity_b: Kindle Paperwhite E-reader (Previous Generation - 7th) - Black, 6" High-Resolution Display (300 ppi) with Built-in Light, Wi-Fi + Free Cellular Connectivity - Includes Special Offers

Jaybird X4 Wireless Bluetooth Headphones for Sport Fitness and Running, Compatible with iOS and Android Smartphones: Sweatproof and Waterproof - Black Metallic/Flash These are very good Bluetooth earbuds for sports use. Construction is very lightweight, but still very durable. Earpieces are very secure when I'm running or working out at the gym and more than comfortable enough for hour-long workouts. Sound quality is pretty good out-of-the-box, but a little thin at the higher frequencies (especially noticeable with acoustic music). Fortunately, Jaybird has a great smartphone app you can use to equalize the sound. I was never very good at designing my own equalization profiles by ear, but the app has several ready made profiles so I just picked the one that sounded best with my favorite music (boosting higher frequencies more than lower frequencies). There is no noise cancellation, but noise isolation is very good with the included foam eartips (not the default eartips).

I really do not like that you need a special dongle to recharge this headset. You can't just plug a standard USB cable directly into these, like with most Bluetooth headset. This may have something to do with the headset's waterproof rating, but other headsets I own are also waterproof and can still be recharged with a standard cable. I am concerned that the proprietary charging dongle will get lost or broken or I will just forget to bring it with me when traveling.

Bluetooth Headband Headphones, Starry Sleep Mask with Bluetooth Headphones Sleep Headphone Bluetooth Headband with Thin Speaker Handsfree Gadgets Best Gift Ideas (Green-1) When this arrived, I immediately put it to use. I have earbuds on me 24/7, even if they aren't in my ears. Sometimes I use them when I am out in public because I have sensory issues and can become easily overstimulated in crowd situations. This arrived in the evening, so I wore it around the house and decided to try wearing them while sleeping.

The band fits my head perfectly, without discomfort. I am a side-sleeper, so there were a few times throughout the night when I could feel the speaker between my ear and the pillow, but it wasn't unbearably uncomfortable (certainly not as uncomfortable as having an in-ear earbud in the ear I am lying on). It was more noticeable because it was a new sensation that I was unaccustomed to. After wearing it for the whole night, I forgot I had it on.

It came with a full charge, which lasted about a day and a half. I haven't recharged it yet, but the care and use instructions that came with it were detailed, clear, and easy to understand. I plan to plug it in tonight and I don't anticipate having any issues.

I will definitely recommend this to friends.

text_fidelity_a:
Amped REC15A Wireless High Power Compact 802.11AC Wi-Fi Range Extender Among the wireless extenders, I have used, this model from Amped has been the easiest to set up, and it works as good as advertised. Using an iPad, it took less than 5 minutes to set up. Very intuitive and well-thought through interface for setting up with very clear information on each screen (an accurate countdown warns you exactly when to expect next steps, etc.). Overall, this has been the most pleasant experience in setting up any electronics gadget that is device-agnostic.

The performance is excellent; in a far away sunroom, the extender easily resulted in a "full" indicator for WiFi devices, and the ethernet port enabled to connect a gaming device (for very infrequent use, this will work very well; I already have an extended port to connect to the TV). The extender has performed consistently as well, no pauses in video streaming, for example.

There is one minor disadvantage, other than what seems to be a tad pricey - the bulk of the unit. It is difficult to place this in plug points with tight corners or abutting walls. I have had mixed experience in trying to print from a device connected to the extended network to a printer on the original network (need to verify settings and will update the review). Overall, an excellent choice for an extender+port option that is extremely easy to set up and works consistently.
text_fidelity_b: Amped REC15A Wireless High Power Compact 802.11AC Wi-Fi Range Extender

text_fidelity_a:
ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger This timer is a good size with a very readable LED display and a strong magnet on the clip on the back to hold it to your fridge or whatever a magnet will stick to. The buttons are large and accessible, and it's really no problem to set it up. It beeps loudly when the time is up, so there's little danger you're not going to hear it from an adjoining room.

Strangely, on day one (unlike with some timers I've used), the first three or four times that I held down the hour, minute, or second buttons to speed up the counting and turn off the beeps, it just froze and stopped counting. If I pressed the button over and over to advance the counter by one, it worked—beeping annoyingly loudly each time, of course. I was about to give it a two-star review and throw it away because I couldn't stand it, but I put off doing it and just stuck it to the top of my stove. A week later, after I'd used the stove several times and the timer probably got exposed to some heat, I went back to try it again so I could write this review and the fast-count sans beeps feature worked. Weird. Maybe it was just stressed in shipping and needed time to settle down....

A few things I really do dislike is that it's easy to reset the time by mistake if the grey button on the left gets slid up; the modes are manually set with this button. (That approach to the modes could be good for the technologically challenged, though.) Also, if you overshoot your mark on the time, there is no way to go backward; you have to go forward until you come back around to where you were supposed to have stopped the first time. The clip is a little too sharply angled, so when you stick the timer to a surface with the magnet, the face slants down somewhat, but it's still visible; really not that big of a deal.

Another thing, as I've remarked about another MeasuPro product: the how-to info on the packaging is white letters on light grey, which is practically unreadable for anyone, not just people like me with old eyes. (The company told me they were correcting that with the other product, so I expect they will do the same with this one.)
text_fidelity_b: ETUCRAY Headphone Jack Adapter for Phone Dongle Aux Audio to 3.5mm Cables Earphone Adaptor Headset Splitter for Music&Charger

StarTech.com SATA to USB Cable - USB 3.0 to 2.5” SATA III Hard Drive Adapter - External Converter for SSD/HDD Data Transfer (USB3S2SAT3CB) I tried this cable with a Samsung EVO 850 240GB drive which I already had tested in a $16.99 Inatek UASB USB 3.0 enclosure (purchased on Amazon).

This UBS 3.1 cable is slower. If you look at the attached photos, the first is the drive with this cable and the 2nd is the exact same drive in the cheap USB 3.0 enclosure. Same computer. This is running the CrystalMark DiskMark 64S benchmarking tool, which is designed to effectively test SSDs.

Disappointing performance. On the plus side, it's certainly simpler to install (the Inatek requires 6 SMALL screws, which is kinda bonkers).
An SSD has no real need of the enclosure. So this seems like it would be a better solution. But not if speed matters.
The benchmark is automatically run 5x and I ran the whole thing twice because I expected this cable to be faster.

I think back to the 42 inch Panasonic Plasma that I bought in 2002 and cringe at the multiple thousands spent. This is a lot of TV for the money. The picture is great. We have a 2012 59 inch top of the line Samsung Plasma and the picture on the Vizio is quite a bit sharper and brighter. It has replaced the Samsung as our go to Blue Ray movie night TV. So to this point we have a TV that is well priced and provides a great picture. So lets move on to the bad. Viewing angle. In our living room a couch sits directly in front of the Vizio. From the couch the picture is AMAZING. Off at about a 35 degree angle sits a recliner and the picture loses a lot of color, brightness and sharpness as viewed from the chair. It is not a horrible picture from the chair but it is quite a difference from straight on. The other is the somewhat slow response from the Vizio smart TV system. Compared to hooking up a Roku the initial start up and response is much slower. Of course if you are going to hook up a Roku then this is no big deal. If you do not have viewing angle concerns and are hooking up a Roku then I think you will absolutely love this amazing bargain.
text_fidelity_b: VIZIO M70-C3 70-Inch Class Ultra HD Full-Array LED Smart TV

text_fidelity_a:
ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK) I've bought and currently use both variants of the Relacon mouse. I'm putting this review on the wireless version.

Overall, 5 stars for the wireless with dongle, 3 stars for the Bluetooth. Unfortunately the Bluetooth one is a bit choppy with tracking, causing the pointer to jump to a random place on the screen often enough to be annoying. The dongle one doesn't have this issue for me. Otherwise they're identical in function and feel.

As a dedicated thumb trackball user since the early 90s, I love it! It is much better quality than any other ambidextrous thumb trackball I've optimistically tried over the years when looking for an alternative to the standard right (or rare left) dedicated handed thumb trackball. I have never been able to get comfortable or quick with finger trackballs, no matter how much I have wanted to or worked at it. Same with the Thinkpad trackpoint.

It is a physical relief to have a mouse that I can use in a neutral wrist position without having my hand or arm stretched out. It is especially nice to be able to transfer and use the mouse with my left hand when I need to type or do something else with my right.

I haven't installed the software or tried to remap the buttons. I just plug in the dongle or pair with Bluetooth, and Windows recognizes it. Since my displays are 1080 or smaller, I keep the speed or acceleration or dpi setting at 1 blink. The button is below the power switch, so I do accidentally tap it occasionally, but it's quick and easy to cycle back to 1.

The stand is more stylish than functional, and even with practice the mouse will sometimes slide right off, but at least it's included. Most of the time, I just switch it off and set the mouse on its side.
text_fidelity_b: ELECOM Relacon Handheld Trackball Mouse, Thumb Control, 2.4GHz Wireless, Ergonomic Design, 10-Button Function with Smooth Tracking, Windows11, MacOS (M-RT1DRBK)
